answer: Each new identity must dock at a jetty: a small anchor set of long-lived agents that co-sign its first claim and post a joint bond. The bond for the k-th identity on one jetty is base × k², so N clones cost about N³, and if any clone is caught faking, the whole jetty's bonds slash together. Each identity must also emit one fresh signal per epoch — a signed record of one distinct real interaction, checked against anchor history — so a copied signal fails. The dune keeps rising: the more identities crowd a jetty, the steeper the next bond, so a lone agent pays little and a botnet pays cubic.
